title: NHIS Health Inequality Trends
summary: Harmonized 16 NHIS survey years (647K+ records) for a health-inequality trends study, with reproducible pipelines and automated checks that caught failures before analysis.
overview: A long-running health-inequality trends study needs data that means the same thing across decades of survey redesigns. I built the harmonization and analysis infrastructure for it: cross-year variable mappings, reproducible pipelines and automated quality checks. The work supports a manuscript in preparation.
myRole: I led the harmonization and analytic workflow in coordination with the faculty investigator, from codebook design to pipeline automation and quality assurance.

sections.title: Data Harmonization & Reproducibility
content: Harmonized variables across 16 NHIS survey years (647K+ records), documenting every cross-year mapping in a codebook.
Built reproducible SAS, R and SQL pipelines across 27 NHIS and NHANES survey waves (1997–2024), cutting the manual analysis cycle from 14 days to 2.

Built automated drift, cross-tabulation and missing-data checks into the pipeline, which caught 3 documented failures, including cross-version inconsistencies and drift from the NHIS survey redesign, before analysis.

outcomes: Harmonized 16 NHIS survey years into an analysis-ready, documented resource.
Cut the manual analysis cycle from 14 days to 2 with reproducible pipelines.
Caught 3 documented data failures before they reached analysis.
